pool.q: What is the most common cause of endogenous endophthalmitis in Asia?
pool.rationale:
Klebsiella pneumoniae

A wide range of bacteria can cause endogenous bacterial endophthalmitis. In North America, 40% of cases occur in patients with endocarditis, most typically caused by Staphylococcus or Streptococcus species. In contrast, 60% of endogenous endophthalmitis cases in Asia occur in patients with liver abscesses caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae. Nearly one-third of cases occur in patients who have urinary tract infections, most often caused by E coli.

pool.q: A 30-year-old woman with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy is worried about losing vision. What condition most acutely increases her risk of progression?
pool.rationale: Women with diabetic retinopathy must be carefully monitored during pregnancy due to the association of pregnancy with worsening retinopathy. Chronic hypertension increases the risk of progression, and the United Kingdom Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) study, which followed patients for an average of 10 years, demonstrated that intensive blood pressure control lowered this risk. Anemia and advanced diabetic nephropathy are viewed as potential markers of advanced diabetic retinopathy.

pool.q: What is the most common complication of pars plana vitrectomy?
pool.rationale: The most common complication of pars plana vitrectomy is visually significant nuclear sclerotic cataract, developing in more than 90% of patients over 50 years of age. Retinal tears occur in less than 5% of pars plana vitrectomy cases. Intraoperative choroidal hemorrhage occurs in less than 1% of cases. Bacterial endophthalmitis occurs in approximately 1 out of 2,000 cases.

pool.q: What drug is associated with cystoid macular edema that does not leak or stain on fundus fluorescein angiogram?
pool.rationale: Nicotinic acid, a treatment for elevated cholesterol and triglycerides, in rare cases characteristically causes a cystoid macular edema that demonstrates no leakage or staining on fundus fluorescein angiography. Fingolimod, a drug used to treat multiple sclerosis, can cause conventional cystoid macular edema with typical late leakage in a “petaloid,” or flower-shaped, pattern. Similarly, rosiglitazone, a newer oral hypoglycemic agent, may cause conventional cystoid macular edema that may be confused with diabetic macular edema. Latanoprost may also be associated with angiographically positive cystoid macular edema.

pool.q: What is the most common cause of dense vitreous hemorrhages?
pool.rationale: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy is the most common cause of dense spontaneous vitreous hemorrhages. Retinal venous occlusions and sickle cell anemia are less common causes of spontaneous vitreous hemorrhage. Posterior vitreous separation, a common occurrence, is not typically associated with a dense vitreous hemorrhage.

pool.q: After 15 years of diabetes mellitus and hypertension, a 62-year-old phakic man complains of 6 months of blurred vision in his right eye. Abnormalities are noted on his fundus and fluorescein angiographic evaluations as shown. What is his most likely diagnosis?
pool.rationale: The fundus has hard exudates in the macula of the right eye. The early fluorescein angiography (FA) images confirm the presence of vascular leakage and areas of capillary nonperfusion in the macula. Later images show a cystoid pattern of leakage. These findings are most consistent with diabetic macular edema. Hypertension-related retinal lesions include cotton-wool spots, microaneurysms, intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMAs), blot hemorrhages, lipid exudates (sometimes referred to as hard exudates) venous beading, and new retinal vessels. FA patterns of choroidal neovascularization may include classic or occult CNV or combinations of both. Classic CNV is an area of bright, lacy, and well-defined hyperfluorescence that is identified in the early phase and progressively leaks by the late phases. Occult CNV can present as late leakage from an unidentifiable source. Fluorescein angiography is relatively resistant to the optical effects of a cataract. Advanced cataract would decrease overall image quality. It is important for a cataract surgeon evaluating a diabetic patient with cataract to carefully consider diabetic retinopathy as an alternative cause of decreased vision.
